Sabbath@Exo.16.23-Heb.description: The Sabbath, meaning "rest," was the seventh day of the week, set apart by God as a holy day for rest and worship (<ref="Exodus 20:8-11; Leviticus 23:3">Exodus 20:8-11; Leviticus 23:3</ref>).
Sabbath@Exo.16.23-Heb.name: Sabbath

Sabtah@Gen.10.7-1Ch.description: Sabtah (or Sabta) was a son of Cush and a grandson of Ham, mentioned in the Table of Nations.
Sabtah@Gen.10.7-1Ch.name: Sabtah

Sabteca@Gen.10.7-1Ch.description: Sabteca was a son of Cush and a grandson of Ham, mentioned in the Table of Nations.
Sabteca@Gen.10.7-1Ch.name: Sabteca

Sachar@1Ch.26.4.description: Sachar was a son of Obed-edom and a Levitical gatekeeper during the reign of King David.
Sachar@1Ch.26.4.name: Sachar

Sachia@1Ch.8.10.description: Sachia was a son of Shaharaim, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin.
Sachia@1Ch.8.10.name: Sachia

Sadducee@Mat.3.7-Act.description: The Sadducees were a Jewish sect that denied the resurrection, angels, and spirits, and often clashed with Jesus and the early church (<ref="Matthew 22:23; Act.23.6-8">Matthew 22:23; Act.23.6-8</ref>).
Sadducee@Mat.3.7-Act.name: Sadducee

Sahar@Ezk.27.18.description: Sahar is a place mentioned in Ezekiel's prophecy, but its exact location is unknown (<ref="Ezk. 27:18">Ezk. 27:18</ref>).
Sahar@Ezk.27.18.name: Sahar

Salamis@Act.13.5.description: Salamis was a city on the island of Cyprus where Paul and Barnabas preached the gospel in the Jewish synagogues (<ref="Act.13.5">Act.13.5</ref>).
Salamis@Act.13.5.name: Salamis

Salecah@Deu.3.10-1Ch.description: Salecah was a city in the region of Bashan, east of the Jordan River, associated with the kingdoms of Og and Sihon (<ref="Deut. 3:10; Josh. 12:5; 13:11; 1Chr. 5:11">Deut. 3:10; Josh. 12:5; 13:11; 1Chr. 5:11</ref>).
Salecah@Deu.3.10-1Ch.name: Salecah

Salim@Jhn.3.23.description: Salim was a place near Aenon where John the Baptist was baptizing, because there was plenty of water there (<ref="Jhn.3.23">Jhn.3.23</ref>).
Salim@Jhn.3.23.name: Salim

Sallai@Neh.11.8.description: Sallai was a Benjamite who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile, as recorded in Nehemiah 11.
Sallai@Neh.11.8.name: Sallai

Sallu@1Ch.9.7.description: Sallu was a Benjamite who lived in Jerusalem, as recorded in the genealogy of 1Chronicles 9.
Sallu@1Ch.9.7.name: Sallu

Sallu@Neh.11.7.description: Sallu was a Benjamite leader who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile, as recorded in Nehemiah 11.
Sallu@Neh.11.7.name: Sallu

Sallu@Neh.12.7-.description: Sallu (or Sallai) was a priest who returned from the Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel and later signed the covenant under Nehemiah.
Sallu@Neh.12.7-.name: Sallu

Salma@1Ch.2.51-.description: Salma was the son of Hur and the  father (ie founder) of Bethlehem, as mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.
Salma@1Ch.2.51-.name: Salma

Salmon@Rut.4.20-Luk.description: Salmon (or Sala) was the son of Nahshon and husband of Rahab - an ancestor of King David and Jesus Christ.
Salmon@Rut.4.20-Luk.name: Salmon

Salmone@Act.27.7.description: Salmone was a promontory on the island of Crete that Paul's ship passed on his voyage to Rome (<ref="Act.27.7">Act.27.7</ref>).
Salmone@Act.27.7.name: Salmone

Salome@Mat.14.6.description: Salome, the daughter of Herodias, danced before Herod and requested the execution of John the Baptist.
Salome@Mat.14.6.name: Salome

Salome@Mat.20.20-Mrk.description: Salome was one of the women who witnessed Jesus' crucifixion and resurrection. She was perhaps the wife of Zebedee.
Salome@Mat.20.20-Mrk.name: Salome

Salt_Sea@Gen.14.3-2Ki.description: The Salt Sea, also known as the Sea of Arabah, is another name for the Dead Sea, located at the lowest point on Earth (<ref="Gen. 14:3; Num. 34:3, 12; Deut. 3:17; Josh. 3:16; 12:3; 15:2, 5; 18:19; Deut. 4:49; 2Ki. 14:25">Gen. 14:3; Num. 34:3, 12; Deut. 3:17; Josh. 3:16; 12:3; 15:2, 5; 18:19; Deut. 4:49; 2Ki. 14:25</ref>).
Salt_Sea@Gen.14.3-2Ki.name: Salt_Sea

Salt_Valley@2Sa.8.13-Psa.description: The Salt Valley was a location where David and his commanders defeated the Edomites and Arameans (<ref="2Sa. 8:13; 2Ki. 14:7; 1Chr. 18:12; 2Chr. 25:11; Psa. 60:1">2Sa. 8:13; 2Ki. 14:7; 1Chr. 18:12; 2Chr. 25:11; Psa. 60:1</ref>).
Salt_Valley@2Sa.8.13-Psa.name: Salt_Valley

Salu@Num.25.14.description: Salu was the father of Zimri, a Simeonite prince who was killed by Phinehas for his involvement with a Midianite woman.
Salu@Num.25.14.name: Salu

Samaria@1Ki.13.32-Act.description: Samaria was the capital city of the northern kingdom of Israel, and its inhabitants were known as Samaritans (<ref="1Ki. 16:24; 2Ki. 17:24; Jhn. 4:9; Act.8.5">1Ki. 16:24; 2Ki. 17:24; Jhn. 4:9; Act.8.5</ref>).
Samaria@1Ki.13.32-Act.name: Samaria

Samgar@Jer.39.3.description: Samgar was a Babylonian official present at the fall of Jerusalem, as recorded in the book of Jeremiah.
Samgar@Jer.39.3.name: Samgar

Samlah@Gen.36.36-1Ch.description: Samlah was a king of Edom who reigned before Israel had kings, as mentioned in the genealogies of Esau.
Samlah@Gen.36.36-1Ch.name: Samlah

Samos@Act.20.15.description: Samos is an island in the Aegean Sea where Paul stopped during his third missionary journey (<ref="Act.20.15">Act.20.15</ref>).
Samos@Act.20.15.name: Samos

Samothrace@Act.16.11.description: Samothrace is an island in the Aegean Sea where Paul and his companions landed during his second missionary journey (<ref="Act.16.11">Act.16.11</ref>).
Samothrace@Act.16.11.name: Samothrace

Samson@Jdg.13.24-Heb.description: Samson was an Israelite judge known for his God-given strength, which he used to fight against the Philistines.
Samson@Jdg.13.24-Heb.name: Samson

Samuel@1Sa.1.20-Heb.description: Samuel was a prophet and the last judge of Israel before the establishment of the monarchy, who anointed both Saul and David as kings.
Samuel@1Sa.1.20-Heb.name: Samuel

Sanballat@Neh.2.10-.description: Sanballat was the governor of Samaria who opposed Nehemiah's efforts to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem.
Sanballat@Neh.2.10-.name: Sanballat

Sansannah@Jos.15.31.description: Sansannah was a town allotted to the tribe of Judah in the Negev region (<ref="Josh. 15:31">Josh. 15:31</ref>).
Sansannah@Jos.15.31.name: Sansannah

Saph@2Sa.21.18-1Ch.description: Saph (or Sippai) was a Philistine giant who was killed by Sibbechai the Hushathite during a battle with the Philistines.
Saph@2Sa.21.18-1Ch.name: Saph

Sapphira@Act.5.1.description: Sapphira, along with her husband Ananias, lied to the apostles about the proceeds from a property sale and died as a result.
Sapphira@Act.5.1.name: Sapphira

Sarah@Gen.11.29-1Pe.description: Sarah (or Sarai) was the wife of Abraham and the mother of Isaac, through whom God fulfilled His promise to make Abraham a great nation.
Sarah@Gen.11.29-1Pe.name: Sarah

Saraph@1Ch.4.22.description: Saraph was a son of Shelah and a descendant of Judah, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.
Saraph@1Ch.4.22.name: Saraph

Sarid@Jos.19.10-.description: Sarid was a border town in the territory allotted to the tribe of Zebulun (<ref="Josh. 19:10, 12">Josh. 19:10, 12</ref>).
Sarid@Jos.19.10-.name: Sarid

Satan@Deu.13.13-Rev.description: Satan, meaning "adversary" or "accuser," is the devil, the chief enemy of God and tempter of humanity, who seeks to hinder God's purposes and lead people into sin (<ref="Job.1.6-12; Matthew 4:1-11; Revelation 12:9">Job.1.6-12; Matthew 4:1-11; Revelation 12:9</ref>).
Satan@Deu.13.13-Rev.name: Satan

Saul@1Sa.9.2-Act.description: Saul was the first king of Israel, anointed by the prophet Samuel, who initially followed God but later disobeyed and was rejected as king.
Saul@1Sa.9.2-Act.name: Saul

Sceva@Act.19.14.description: Sceva was a Jewish chief priest whose seven sons attempted to exorcise demons in the name of Jesus, as mentioned in the book of Acts.
Sceva@Act.19.14.name: Sceva

Scythians@Col.3.11.description: The Scythians were a nomadic people group known for their barbaric reputation.
Scythians@Col.3.11.name: Scythians

Seba@Gen.10.7-1Ch.description: Seba was a son of Cush and brother of Raamah.
Seba@Gen.10.7-1Ch.name: Seba

Seba@Psa.72.10-Isa.description: Seba was a kingdom mentioned in prophetic and poetic texts, often in the context of bringing gifts to God (<ref="Psa. 72:10; Isa. 43:3">Psa. 72:10; Isa. 43:3</ref>).
Seba@Psa.72.10-Isa.name: Seba

Sebam@Num.32.3.description: Sebam was one of the towns in the territory of Reuben, east of the Jordan River (<ref="Num. 32:3">Num. 32:3</ref>).
Sebam@Num.32.3.name: Sebam

Secacah@Jos.15.61.description: Secacah was a town located in the wilderness region of Judah (<ref="Josh. 15:61">Josh. 15:61</ref>).
Secacah@Jos.15.61.name: Secacah

Second_Quarter@2Ki.22.14-Zep.description: The Second Quarter was a district in Jerusalem mentioned in connection with the prophetess Huldah (<ref="2Ki. 22:14; 2Chr. 34:22">2Ki. 22:14; 2Chr. 34:22</ref>) and in Zephaniah's prophecy (<ref="Zeph. 1:10">Zeph. 1:10</ref>).
Second_Quarter@2Ki.22.14-Zep.name: Second_Quarter

Secu@1Sa.19.22.description: Secu was a place near Ramah where Saul went in search of David (<ref="1Sam. 19:22">1Sam. 19:22</ref>).
Secu@1Sa.19.22.name: Secu

Secundus@Act.20.4.description: Secundus was a Thessalonian believer who accompanied Paul on his journey.
Secundus@Act.20.4.name: Secundus

Segub@1Ch.2.21-.description: Segub, son of Hezron, was the father of Jair, who had twenty-three cities in Gilead.
Segub@1Ch.2.21-.name: Segub

Segub@1Ki.16.34.description: Segub was the son of Hiel, who rebuilt Jericho during Ahab's reign.
Segub@1Ki.16.34.name: Segub

Seir@Gen.14.6-Ezk.description: Seir was a mountainous region inhabited by the Edomites, the descendants of Esau (<ref="Gen. 32:3; 36:8; Num. 24:18; Deut. 2:4; Josh. 24:4">Gen. 32:3; 36:8; Num. 24:18; Deut. 2:4; Josh. 24:4</ref>).
Seir@Gen.14.6-Ezk.name: Seir

Seir@Gen.36.20-1Ch.description: Seir was a Horite chief and an ancestor of the Horites who inhabited the land of Seir.
Seir@Gen.36.20-1Ch.name: Seir

Seir_Mount@Deu.1.2-Ezk.description: Mount Seir refers to the mountainous region within Seir, often associated with the Edomites (<ref="Deut. 1:2; 2:1, 5; 1Chr. 4:42; Ezek. 35:2, 3, 7, 15">Deut. 1:2; 2:1, 5; 1Chr. 4:42; Ezek. 35:2, 3, 7, 15</ref>).
Seir_Mount@Deu.1.2-Ezk.name: Seir_Mount

Seir_Mount@Jos.15.10.description: Mount Seir was a landmark on the boundary of Judah, near Kiriath-jearim and Chesalon (<ref="Josh. 15:10">Josh. 15:10</ref>).
Seir_Mount@Jos.15.10.name: Seir_Mount

Seirah@Jdg.3.26.description: Seirah was the place to which Ehud escaped after killing Eglon, the king of Moab (<ref="Judg. 3:26">Judg. 3:26</ref>).
Seirah@Jdg.3.26.name: Seirah

Sela@Jdg.1.36-Isa.description: Sela, also known as rock or Joktheel, was an Edomite stronghold captured by King Amaziah of Judah (<ref="2Ki. 14:7; 2Chr. 25:12; Isa. 16:1; 42:11; Judg. 1:36">2Ki. 14:7; 2Chr. 25:12; Isa. 16:1; 42:11; Judg. 1:36</ref>).
Sela@Jdg.1.36-Isa.name: Sela

Selah@Psa.3.2-Hab.description: Selah is a term frequently used in the Psalms and Habakkuk, likely a musical or liturgical direction, though its precise meaning is uncertain (<ref="Psalm 3:2, 4, 8; Habakkuk 3:3, 9, 13">Psalm 3:2, 4, 8; Habakkuk 3:3, 9, 13</ref>).
Selah@Psa.3.2-Hab.name: Selah

Seled@1Ch.2.30.description: Seled, a son of Nadab, died without having any children.
Seled@1Ch.2.30.name: Seled

Seleucia@Act.13.4.description: Seleucia was the port city from which Paul and Barnabas sailed to Cyprus on their first missionary journey (<ref="Act.13.4">Act.13.4</ref>).
Seleucia@Act.13.4.name: Seleucia

Semachiah@1Ch.26.7.description: Semachiah, a son of Shemaiah, served as a gatekeeper in the temple during the time of David.
Semachiah@1Ch.26.7.name: Semachiah

Semein@Luk.3.26.description: Semein is mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus Christ, as recorded in Luke's Gospel.
Semein@Luk.3.26.name: Semein

Senaah@Ezr.2.35-Neh.description: Senaah was a town whose people are listed among those who returned to Judah from the Babylonian exile (<ref="Ezr. 2:35; Neh. 7:38">Ezr. 2:35; Neh. 7:38</ref>).
Senaah@Ezr.2.35-Neh.name: Senaah

Seneh@1Sa.14.4.description: Seneh was one of two rocky crags between which Jonathan and his armor-bearer passed to attack the Philistine garrison at Michmash (<ref="1Sam. 14:4">1Sam. 14:4</ref>).
Seneh@1Sa.14.4.name: Seneh

Sennacherib@2Ki.18.13-Isa.description: Sennacherib and Sargon were Assyrian kings who led military campaigns against Judah during the reigns of King Hezekiah and King Ahaz, respectively.
Sennacherib@2Ki.18.13-Isa.name: Sennacherib

Seorim@1Ch.24.8.description: Seorim was a priest who served during David's reign and was the head of the fourth priestly division.
Seorim@1Ch.24.8.name: Seorim

Sephar@Gen.10.30.description: Sephar was a mountain in the east that marked the boundary of the territory settled by the descendants of Joktan (<ref="Gen. 10:30">Gen. 10:30</ref>).
Sephar@Gen.10.30.name: Sephar

Sepharad@Oba.1.20-Rev.description: Sepharad, possibly referring to Sardis, was a destination of exiled Jews (<ref="Obad. 1:20">Obad. 1:20</ref>) and one of the seven churches mentioned in Revelation (<ref="Rev. 1:11; 3:1, 4">Rev. 1:11; 3:1, 4</ref>).
Sepharad@Oba.1.20-Rev.name: Sepharad

Sepharvaim@2Ki.17.24-Isa.description: Sepharvaim was one of the cities from which the Assyrians brought people to resettle in Samaria after the deportation of the Israelites (<ref="2Ki. 17:24, 31; 18:34; 19:13; Isa. 36:19; 37:13">2Ki. 17:24, 31; 18:34; 19:13; Isa. 36:19; 37:13</ref>).
Sepharvaim@2Ki.17.24-Isa.name: Sepharvaim

Serah@Gen.46.17-1Ch.description: Serah was the daughter of Asher and the sister of Asher's sons, as mentioned in the genealogies of the tribe of Asher.
Serah@Gen.46.17-1Ch.name: Serah

Seraiah@1Ch.4.13-.description: Seraiah, the son of Kenaz, was the father of Joab, who was the father of the Valley of Craftsmen.
Seraiah@1Ch.4.13-.name: Seraiah

Seraiah@1Ch.4.35.description: Seraiah, the son of Asiel, was a descendant of Simeon mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Simeon.
Seraiah@1Ch.4.35.name: Seraiah

Seraiah@2Ki.25.18-Jer.description: Seraiah served as the high priest during the reign of King Zedekiah and was executed by the Babylonians after the fall of Jerusalem.
Seraiah@2Ki.25.18-Jer.name: Seraiah

Seraiah@2Ki.25.23-Jer.description: Seraiah, the son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, was one of the officers who served under Gedaliah, the governor appointed by the Babylonians after the fall of Jerusalem.
Seraiah@2Ki.25.23-Jer.name: Seraiah

Seraiah@2Sa.8.17-1Ch.description: Seraiah, also known as Shavsha, Sheva, Sheya, or Shisha, served as David's scribe during his reign.
Seraiah@2Sa.8.17-1Ch.name: Seraiah

Seraiah@Ezr.2.2-Neh.description: Seraiah was a priest who returned from the Babylonian exile and is mentioned in the lists of returning exiles and priests.
Seraiah@Ezr.2.2-Neh.name: Seraiah

Seraiah@Jer.36.26.description: Seraiah, the son of Azriel, was one of the men sent by King Jehoiakim to capture Jeremiah and Baruch.
Seraiah@Jer.36.26.name: Seraiah

Seraiah@Jer.51.59-.description: Seraiah, the son of Neriah and brother of Baruch, accompanied King Zedekiah to Babylon and carried a message from Jeremiah.
Seraiah@Jer.51.59-.name: Seraiah

Sered@Gen.46.14-Num.description: Sered was a son of Zebulun and the ancestor of the Seredite clan.
Sered@Gen.46.14-Num.name: Sered

Sergius_Paulus@Act.13.7.description: Sergius Paulus, the proconsul of Cyprus, was an intelligent man who sought to hear the word of God and believed after witnessing Paul's confrontation with Elymas the sorcerer.
Sergius_Paulus@Act.13.7.name: Sergius_Paulus

Serug@Gen.11.20-Luk.description: Serug was the son of Reu, the father of Nahor, and an ancestor of Abraham, living to the age of 230 years.
Serug@Gen.11.20-Luk.name: Serug

Seth@Gen.4.25-Luk.description: Seth was the third son of Adam and Eve, born after the death of Abel, and became the ancestor of the righteous line of humanity.
Seth@Gen.4.25-Luk.name: Seth

Sethur@Num.13.13.description: Sethur, the son of Michael, was one of the twelve spies sent by Moses to scout out the land of Canaan, representing the tribe of Asher.
Sethur@Num.13.13.name: Sethur

Shaalbim@Jos.19.42-1Ch.description: Shaalbim, also called Shaalabbin, was a town allotted to the tribe of Dan (<ref="Josh. 19:42; Judg. 1:35">Josh. 19:42; Judg. 1:35</ref>) and the hometown of some of David's mighty men (<ref="2Sam. 23:32; 1Chr. 11:33">2Sam. 23:32; 1Chr. 11:33</ref>). It was also a town under Solomon's administration (<ref="1Ki. 4:9">1Ki. 4:9</ref>).
Shaalbim@Jos.19.42-1Ch.name: Shaalbim

Shaalim@1Sa.9.4.description: Shaalim was a region through which Saul passed while searching for his father's lost donkeys (<ref="1Sam. 9:4">1Sam. 9:4</ref>).
Shaalim@1Sa.9.4.name: Shaalim

Shaaph@1Ch.2.47.description: Shaaph, a son of Jahdai, was a descendant of Caleb.
Shaaph@1Ch.2.47.name: Shaaph

Shaaph@1Ch.2.49.description: Shaaph, a son of Caleb's concubine Maacah, was the father of Madmannah.
Shaaph@1Ch.2.49.name: Shaaph

Shaaraim@Jos.15.36-1Sa.description: Shaaraim was a town in the Shephelah of Judah (<ref="Josh. 15:36">Josh. 15:36</ref>) and a place the Philistines passed in their retreat from Socoh (<ref="1Sam. 17:52">1Sam. 17:52</ref>).
Shaaraim@Jos.15.36-1Sa.name: Shaaraim

Shaashgaz@Est.2.14.description: Shaashgaz was the eunuch appointed by King Ahasuerus to be in charge of the concubines in the royal harem.
Shaashgaz@Est.2.14.name: Shaashgaz

Shabbethai@Ezr.10.15.description: Shabbethai, a Levite, opposed Ezra's efforts to address the issue of intermarriage among the returned exiles.
Shabbethai@Ezr.10.15.name: Shabbethai

Shabbethai@Neh.11.16.description: Shabbethai, a Levite, was responsible for overseeing external affairs in Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah.
Shabbethai@Neh.11.16.name: Shabbethai

Shabbethai@Neh.8.7.description: Shabbethai, a Levite, assisted in explaining the Law to the people during the public reading led by Ezra.
Shabbethai@Neh.8.7.name: Shabbethai

Shaharaim@1Ch.8.8.description: Shaharaim, a Benjamite, had two wives, Hushim and Baara, and he sent them away.
Shaharaim@1Ch.8.8.name: Shaharaim

Shahazumah@Jos.19.22.description: Shahazumah was a town on the border of Issachar's territory (<ref="Josh. 19:22">Josh. 19:22</ref>).
Shahazumah@Jos.19.22.name: Shahazumah

Shalishah@1Sa.9.4.description: Shalishah was a region Saul and his servant passed through while searching for his father's lost donkeys (<ref="1Sam. 9:4">1Sam. 9:4</ref>).
Shalishah@1Sa.9.4.name: Shalishah

Shallecheth@1Ch.26.16.description: Shallecheth was a gate in Jerusalem assigned to the Levites Shuppim and Hosah for guard duty (<ref="1Chr. 26:16">1Chr. 26:16</ref>).
Shallecheth@1Ch.26.16.name: Shallecheth

Shallum@1Ch.2.40-.description: Shallum, the son of Sismai, was a descendant of Judah through the line of Jerahmeel.
Shallum@1Ch.2.40-.name: Shallum

Shallum@1Ch.3.15.description: Shallum was a son of Josiah, king of Judah, and the brother of Jehoiakim and Zedekiah.
Shallum@1Ch.3.15.name: Shallum

Shallum@1Ch.4.25.description: Shallum was the son of Shaul and a descendant of Simeon.
Shallum@1Ch.4.25.name: Shallum

Shallum@1Ch.6.12-Neh.description: Shallum, also known as Meshullam, was a high priest during the time of the kings of Judah, serving as the son of Zadok and the father of Hilkiah.
Shallum@1Ch.6.12-Neh.name: Shallum

Shallum@1Ch.9.17-Neh.description: Shallum was a gatekeeper of the tabernacle during the reign of David, and his descendants continued to serve as gatekeepers in the temple.
Shallum@1Ch.9.17-Neh.name: Shallum

Shallum@2Ch.28.12.description: Shallum, along with other leaders from Ephraim, opposed the army of Israel taking captives from Judah during the reign of King Ahaz.
Shallum@2Ch.28.12.name: Shallum

Shallum@2Ki.15.10-.description: Shallum, son of Jabesh, conspired against Zechariah, king of Israel, assassinated him, and succeeded him as king, reigning for one month.
Shallum@2Ki.15.10-.name: Shallum

Shallum@2Ki.22.14-2Ch.description: Shallum, the husband of Huldah the prophetess, was the keeper of the wardrobe during the reign of King Josiah.
Shallum@2Ki.22.14-2Ch.name: Shallum

Shallum@Ezr.10.24.description: Shallum was one of the singers who had married a foreign woman and agreed to put her away during Ezra's reforms.
Shallum@Ezr.10.24.name: Shallum

Shallum@Ezr.10.42.description: Shallum was one of the Israelites who had married a foreign woman and pledged to put her away during Ezra's reforms.
Shallum@Ezr.10.42.name: Shallum

Shallum@Jer.32.7.description: Shallum was the uncle of Jeremiah the prophet and the father of Hanamel, who sold a field to Jeremiah.
Shallum@Jer.32.7.name: Shallum

Shallum@Jer.35.4.description: Shallum was the father of Maaseiah, who was a keeper of the threshold during the time of Jeremiah the prophet.
Shallum@Jer.35.4.name: Shallum

Shallum@Neh.3.12.description: Shallum, the son of Hallohesh and ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, repaired a section of the city wall along with his daughters.
Shallum@Neh.3.12.name: Shallum

Shallum@Neh.3.15.description: Shallum, the son of Col-hozeh and ruler of the district of Mizpah, repaired the Fountain Gate and the wall of the Pool of Shelah during Nehemiah's rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls.
Shallum@Neh.3.15.name: Shallum

Shalmai@Ezr.2.46-Neh.description: Shalmai (or Shamlai) was an ancestor of the Nethinim, and his descendants were among those who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.
Shalmai@Ezr.2.46-Neh.name: Shalmai

Shalmaneser@2Ki.17.3-Hos.description: Shalmaneser, king of Assyria, besieged Samaria and conquered the northern kingdom of Israel, exiling its inhabitants and ending the kingdom's existence.
Shalmaneser@2Ki.17.3-Hos.name: Shalmaneser

Shama@1Ch.11.44.description: Shama, the son of Hotham the Aroerite, was one of the mighty men in David's army.
Shama@1Ch.11.44.name: Shama

Shamgar@Jdg.3.31-.description: Shamgar, the son of Anath, was a judge of Israel who delivered the nation by killing 600 Philistines with an oxgoad.
Shamgar@Jdg.3.31-.name: Shamgar

Sibmah@Num.32.38-Jer.name: Sibmah

Sibraim@Ezk.47.16.description: Sibraim was a place mentioned by Ezekiel as a landmark on the northeastern border of the Promised Land, between the territory of Damascus and that of Hamath (<ref="Ezek. 47:16">Ezek. 47:16</ref>).
Sibraim@Ezk.47.16.name: Sibraim

Siddim_Valley@Gen.14.3-.description: The Valley of Siddim, located near the Dead Sea, was the site of a battle between the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah and the kings of Elam and their allies (<ref="Gen. 14:3, 8, 10">Gen. 14:3, 8, 10</ref>).
Siddim_Valley@Gen.14.3-.name: Siddim_Valley

Sidon@Gen.10.15-1Ch.description: Sidon was the firstborn son of Canaan and the ancestor of the Sidonian people.
Sidon@Gen.10.15-1Ch.name: Sidon

Sidon@Gen.10.19-Act.description: Sidon, also called Great Sidon, was a prominent Phoenician city known for its trade and culture, and was the hometown of Jezebel, wife of King Ahab (<ref="1Ki. 16:31">1Ki. 16:31</ref>). It is mentioned in various contexts throughout the Bible, including the Old Testament (<ref="Gen. 10:19; Josh. 11:8; Judg. 10:6; Isa. 23:2-4; Jer. 27:3; Ezek. 28:21-22">Gen. 10:19; Josh. 11:8; Judg. 10:6; Isa. 23:2-4; Jer. 27:3; Ezek. 28:21-22</ref>) and the New Testament (<ref="Matt. 11:21-22; Luke 4:26; Act.27.3">Matt. 11:21-22; Luke 4:26; Act.27.3</ref>).
Sidon@Gen.10.19-Act.name: Sidon

Sihon@Num.21.21-Jer.description: Sihon was the Amorite king of Heshbon who refused to let the Israelites pass through his land and was subsequently defeated by them.
Sihon@Num.21.21-Jer.name: Sihon

Sikkuth@Amo.5.26.description: Sikkuth, possibly an Assyrian deity, was one of the pagan gods worshipped by the Israelites, for which they were condemned to exile (<ref="Amo.5.26">Amo.5.26</ref>).
Sikkuth@Amo.5.26.name: Sikkuth

Silas@Act.15.22-1Pe.description: Silas (or Silvanus) was a prominent member of the Jerusalem church who accompanied Paul on his second missionary journey and co-wrote some of his epistles.
Silas@Act.15.22-1Pe.name: Silas

Silla@2Ki.12.20.description: Silla was the place where King Joash of Judah was assassinated by his servants (<ref="2Ki. 12:20">2Ki. 12:20</ref>).
Silla@2Ki.12.20.name: Silla

Simeon@Act.13.1.description: Simeon, also called Niger, was a prophet and teacher in the church at Antioch who was involved in sending Paul and Barnabas on their first missionary journey.
Simeon@Act.13.1.name: Simeon

Simeon@Gen.29.33-Rev.description: Simeon, the second son of Jacob and Leah, was the founder of the tribe of Simeon and played a role in the story of Joseph.
Simeon@Gen.29.33-Rev.name: Simeon

Simeon@Luk.2.25-.description: Simeon was a righteous and devout man in Jerusalem who blessed the infant Jesus in the temple and prophesied about his future.
Simeon@Luk.2.25-.name: Simeon

Simeon@Luk.3.30.description: Simeon is mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus as the son of Judah and the father of Levi.
Simeon@Luk.3.30.name: Simeon

Simon@Act.8.13-.description: Simon was a tanner in Joppa who hosted the apostle Peter in his home.
Simon@Act.8.13-.name: Simon

Simon@Act.8.9-.description: Simon was a sorcerer in Samaria who believed and was baptized but later tried to buy the power of the Holy Spirit from the apostles.
Simon@Act.8.9-.name: Simon

Simon@Jhn.6.71-.description: Simon was the father of Judas Iscariot, the disciple who betrayed Jesus.
Simon@Jhn.6.71-.name: Simon

Simon@Mat.10.4-Act.description: Simon, also known as the Zealot, was one of the twelve apostles chosen by Jesus.
Simon@Mat.10.4-Act.name: Simon

Simon@Mat.13.55-Mrk.description: Simon was one of the brothers of Jesus, a son of Mary and Joseph.
Simon@Mat.13.55-Mrk.name: Simon

Simon@Mat.26.6-Luk.description: Simon the leper was a man in Bethany who hosted a meal for Jesus, during which a woman anointed Jesus with expensive perfume.
Simon@Mat.26.6-Luk.name: Simon

Simon@Mat.27.32-Luk.description: Simon of Cyrene was compelled by Roman soldiers to carry Jesus' cross on the way to his crucifixion.
Simon@Mat.27.32-Luk.name: Simon

Sin@Exo.16.1-Num.description: Sin was a wilderness area between Elim and Sinai where the Israelites camped during their journey from Egypt to the Promised Land (<ref="Exod. 16:1; 17:1; Num. 33:11-12">Exod. 16:1; 17:1; Num. 33:11-12</ref>).
Sin@Exo.16.1-Num.name: Sin

Sinai@Exo.3.1-Gal.description: Sinai, also called Mount Sinai, Horeb, or Mount Horeb, was the mountain where God gave Moses the Ten Commandments and other laws (<ref="Exod. 19-40; Lev. 7:38; 25:1; 26:46; 27:34; Num. 3:1; 28:6; Deut. 33:2; Judg. 5:5; Ps. 68:8, 17; Neh. 9:13; Mal. 4:4; Act.7.30, 38; Gal. 4:24-25">Exod. 19-40; Lev. 7:38; 25:1; 26:46; 27:34; Num. 3:1; 28:6; Deut. 33:2; Judg. 5:5; Ps. 68:8, 17; Neh. 9:13; Mal. 4:4; Act.7.30, 38; Gal. 4:24-25</ref>).
Sinai@Exo.3.1-Gal.name: Sinai

Sinai_Wilderness@Exo.19.1-Num.description: The Sinai Wilderness was the region where the Israelites camped after the Exodus and received the Law.
Sinai_Wilderness@Exo.19.1-Num.name: Sinai_Wilderness

Sinites@Gen.10.17-1Ch.description: The Sinites were a Canaanite people group descended from Canaan, the son of Ham.
Sinites@Gen.10.17-1Ch.name: Sinites

Siphmoth@1Sa.30.28.description: Siphmoth was one of the towns in southern Judah that received a share of the spoils from David after he defeated the Amalekites (<ref="1Sam. 30:28">1Sam. 30:28</ref>).
Siphmoth@1Sa.30.28.name: Siphmoth

Sirah@2Sa.3.26.description: Sirah, also called the Cistern of Sirah, was a place near Hebron where Joab killed Abner in revenge for the death of his brother Asahel (<ref="2Sam. 3:26">2Sam. 3:26</ref>).
Sirah@2Sa.3.26.name: Sirah

Sisera@Ezr.2.53-Neh.description: Sisera was the ancestor of a family of temple servants who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.
Sisera@Ezr.2.53-Neh.name: Sisera

Sisera@Jdg.4.2-Psa.description: Sisera was the commander of the Canaanite army who was defeated by the Israelites under the leadership of Deborah and Barak.
Sisera@Jdg.4.2-Psa.name: Sisera

Sismai@1Ch.2.40.description: Sismai was a descendant of Judah through Jerahmeel, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.
Sismai@1Ch.2.40.name: Sismai

Sithri@Exo.6.22.description: Sithri was a son of Uzziel, a Levite of the Kohathite clan, mentioned in the genealogy of the Levites.
Sithri@Exo.6.22.name: Sithri

Sitnah@Gen.26.21.description: Sitnah was a well dug by Isaac in the Valley of Gerar, but the Philistines disputed its ownership (<ref="Gen. 26:21">Gen. 26:21</ref>).
Sitnah@Gen.26.21.name: Sitnah

Sivan@Est.8.9.description: Sivan is the third month of the Jewish calendar, mentioned in <ref="Esther 8:9">Esther 8:9</ref> as the month in which Mordecai's decree was written and sent to the provinces.
Sivan@Est.8.9.name: Sivan

Smyrna@Rev.1.11-.description: Smyrna was one of the seven churches of Asia Minor addressed in the Book of Revelation, known for its persecution and poverty, yet faithful to Christ (<ref="Rev. 1:11; 2:8-11">Rev. 1:11; 2:8-11</ref>).
Smyrna@Rev.1.11-.name: Smyrna

So@2Ki.17.4.description: So was an Egyptian pharaoh to whom King Hoshea of Israel sent messengers, likely seeking an alliance against Assyria.
So@2Ki.17.4.name: So

Soco@1Ch.4.18.description: Soco was a son of Heber, from the tribe of Judah, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.
Soco@1Ch.4.18.name: Soco

Socoh@Jos.15.35-2Ch.description: Socoh was a town in the Shephelah region of Judah (<ref="Josh. 15:35">Josh. 15:35</ref>), known for being near the site of David's battle with Goliath (<ref="1Sam. 17:1">1Sam. 17:1</ref>) and later fortified by Rehoboam (<ref="2Chr. 11:7">2Chr. 11:7</ref>).
Socoh@Jos.15.35-2Ch.name: Socoh

Socoh@Jos.15.48.description: Socoh, a town allotted to the tribe of Judah in the hill country (<ref="Jos. 15:48">Jos. 15:48</ref>).
Socoh@Jos.15.48.name: Socoh

Sodi@Num.13.10.description: Sodi was the father of Gaddiel, the man chosen from the tribe of Zebulun to spy out the land of Canaan.
Sodi@Num.13.10.name: Sodi

Sodom@Gen.10.19-Rev.description: Sodom, a notoriously wicked city destroyed by God along with Gomorrah for their grave sins (<ref="Gen. 19:24-25">Gen. 19:24-25</ref>).
Sodom@Gen.10.19-Rev.name: Sodom

Solomon's_Portico@Act.3.11-.description: Solomon's Portico, a colonnade in the Jerusalem temple where the apostles gathered to teach (<ref="Act.3.11; 5:12">Act.3.11; 5:12</ref>).
Solomon's_Portico@Act.3.11-.name: Solomon's_Portico

Solomon@2Sa.5.14-Act.description: Solomon, also called Jedidiah, was the son of David and Bathsheba who succeeded his father as king of Israel and was renowned for his wisdom, wealth, and the construction of the First Temple in Jerusalem.
Solomon@2Sa.5.14-Act.name: Solomon

Sopater@Act.20.4-Rom.description: Sopater (or Sosipater) was a companion of Paul from Berea who accompanied him on his journey to Jerusalem and later sent greetings to the church in Rome.
Sopater@Act.20.4-Rom.name: Sopater

Sophereth@Ezr.2.55-Neh.description: Sophereth (or Hassophereth) was the ancestor of a family of Solomon's servants who were among the exiles that returned to Jerusalem from Babylon.
Sophereth@Ezr.2.55-Neh.name: Sophereth

Sorek_Valley@Jdg.16.4.description: Sorek Valley, the place where Delilah lived and where Samson's downfall began (<ref="Judg. 16:4">Judg. 16:4</ref>).
Sorek_Valley@Jdg.16.4.name: Sorek_Valley

Sosthenes@Act.18.17-1Co.description: Sosthenes was a synagogue ruler in Corinth who was beaten by a mob and later became a co-sender of Paul's first letter to the Corinthians.
Sosthenes@Act.18.17-1Co.name: Sosthenes

Sotai@Ezr.2.55-Neh.description: Sotai was the ancestor of a family of Solomon's servants who were among the exiles that returned to Jerusalem from Babylon.
Sotai@Ezr.2.55-Neh.name: Sotai

Spain@Rom.15.24-.description: Spain, a country Paul planned to visit to preach the gospel (<ref="Rom. 15:24, 28">Rom. 15:24, 28</ref>).
Spain@Rom.15.24-.name: Spain

Stachys@Rom.16.9.description: Stachys was a believer in Rome whom Paul greeted as his beloved friend.
Stachys@Rom.16.9.name: Stachys

Stephanas@1Co.1.16-.description: Stephanas was a believer from Corinth who, along with his household, was baptized by Paul and later visited Paul to provide support and encouragement.
Stephanas@1Co.1.16-.name: Stephanas

Stephen@Act.6.5-.description: Stephen, one of the seven deacons chosen by the early church, was full of faith and the Holy Spirit, performed miracles, and became the first Christian martyr after his powerful testimony before the Sanhedrin.
Stephen@Act.6.5-.name: Stephen

Stoic@Act.17.18.description: The Stoics were a Greek philosophical school that emphasized reason, self-control, and the acceptance of fate, some of whom debated with Paul in Athens (<ref="Act.17.18">Act.17.18</ref>).
Stoic@Act.17.18.name: Stoic

Straight@Act.9.11.description: Straight, a street in Damascus where Saul stayed in the house of Judas after his conversion (<ref="Act.9.11">Act.9.11</ref>).
Straight@Act.9.11.name: Straight

Suah@1Ch.7.36.description: Suah, a descendant of Asher mentioned in a genealogy.
Suah@1Ch.7.36.name: Suah

Sucathite@1Ch.2.55.description: The Sucathites were a Kenite clan known for their scribal skills, mentioned in <ref="1Ch.2.55">1Ch.2.55</ref> among the descendants of Salma.
Sucathite@1Ch.2.55.name: Sucathite

Succoth-benoth@2Ki.17.30.description: Succoth-benoth was a Babylonian deity worshipped by the Sepharvites, one of the peoples settled in Samaria by the Assyrian king (<ref="2Ki.17.30">2Ki.17.30</ref>).
Succoth-benoth@2Ki.17.30.name: Succoth-benoth

Succoth@Exo.12.37-Num.description: Succoth, the first place the Israelites camped after leaving Egypt during the Exodus (<ref="Exod. 12:37; Num. 33:5">Exod. 12:37; Num. 33:5</ref>).
Succoth@Exo.12.37-Num.name: Succoth

Succoth@Gen.33.17-Psa.description: Succoth, a city in Canaan allocated to the tribe of Gad, later the site of Solomon's bronze works (<ref="Gen. 33:17; Josh. 13:27; 1Kgs. 7:46">Gen. 33:17; Josh. 13:27; 1Kgs. 7:46</ref>).
Succoth@Gen.33.17-Psa.name: Succoth

Sukkiim@2Ch.12.3.description: The Sukkiim were an African people who joined Shishak's invasion of Judah.
Sukkiim@2Ch.12.3.name: Sukkiim

Suph@Deu.1.1.description: Suph, a place near the wilderness where Moses spoke to the Israelites (<ref="Deut. 1:1">Deut. 1:1</ref>).
Suph@Deu.1.1.name: Suph

Suphah@Num.21.14.description: Suphah, a place mentioned in the Book of the Wars of the Lord (<ref="Num. 21:14">Num. 21:14</ref>).
Suphah@Num.21.14.name: Suphah

Sur@2Ki.11.6.description: Sur, a gate of the temple in Jerusalem, possibly referring to the Foundation Gate (<ref="2Kgs. 11:6">2Kgs. 11:6</ref>).
Sur@2Ki.11.6.name: Sur

Susa@Ezr.4.9-Dan.description: Susa, the capital city of the Persian Empire, where Esther lived and the events of her book took place (<ref="Esth. 1:2; Dan. 8:2">Esth. 1:2; Dan. 8:2</ref>).
Susa@Ezr.4.9-Dan.name: Susa

Susanna@Luk.8.3.description: Susanna was one of the women who provided for Jesus out of her resources.
Susanna@Luk.8.3.name: Susanna

Susi@Num.13.11.description: Susi was the father of Gaddi, the spy from the tribe of Manasseh.
Susi@Num.13.11.name: Susi

Sychar@Jhn.4.5.description: Sychar, a Samaritan city near Jacob's well, where Jesus spoke with a Samaritan woman (<ref="Jhn.4.5">Jhn.4.5</ref>).
Sychar@Jhn.4.5.name: Sychar

Syene@Isa.49.12-Ezk.description: Syene, the southern border of Egypt, mentioned in prophecies about Egypt's destruction (<ref="Ezek. 29:10; 30:6">Ezek. 29:10; 30:6</ref>).
Syene@Isa.49.12-Ezk.name: Syene

Syntyche@Php.4.2.description: Syntyche was a prominent woman in Philippi whom Paul urged to reconcile with Euodia.
Syntyche@Php.4.2.name: Syntyche

Syracuse@Act.28.12.description: Syracuse, a city on the island of Sicily where Paul's ship stopped for three days on his journey to Rome (<ref="Act.28.12">Act.28.12</ref>).
Syracuse@Act.28.12.name: Syracuse

Syria@Jdg.10.6-Gal.description: Syria, an ancient region north of Israel, often engaged in conflicts with Israel and Judah (<ref="1Kgs. 20:1; 2Kgs. 13:3">1Kgs. 20:1; 2Kgs. 13:3</ref>).
Syria@Jdg.10.6-Gal.name: Syria

Syrtis@Act.27.17.description: Syrtis, a dangerous area of shallow waters off the coast of Libya, feared by sailors (<ref="Act.27.17">Act.27.17</ref>).
Syrtis@Act.27.17.name: Syrtis

sister_of_Tahpenes@1Ki.11.19.description: The sister of Tahpenes, an Egyptian queen, was given in marriage to Hadad the Edomite by Pharaoh.
sister_of_Tahpenes@1Ki.11.19.name: sister_of_Tahpenes

son_of_Jashen@2Sa.23.32.description: The son of Jashen, unnamed in the Bible, was one of David's mighty men.
son_of_Jashen@2Sa.23.32.name: son_of_Jashen

son_of_Joiada@Neh.13.28.description: The son of Joiada, a grandson of the high priest Eliashib, married the daughter of Sanballat the Horonite.
son_of_Joiada@Neh.13.28.name: son_of_Joiada
